Worker reporting model (queuing-delay trigger with backlog depth >= 2, kCongestionThreshold=200ms, kCongestionIdleGap=5ms, kLongScriptDuration=5ms, blockingDuration = span - 200ms, scriptCount==0 moments discarded, timer scheduled time = enqueue + delay) transcribed from animation_frame_timing_monitor.cc OnWorkerTaskCompleted/FinalizeCongestedMoment and cross-checked against the WPT worker suite. Slug support-long-animation-frames-api-in-web-workers is the slugified LISTING name 'Support Long Animation Frames API in Web Workers'; the feature id 5387465121726464 was confirmed present in the milestone=153 listing's features_by_type under 'In developer trial (Behind a flag)' by direct API query on 2026-09-13. The developer-facing delta is three items (worker entry capability, scriptCount field, PerformanceScriptTiming worker exposure delta); all three are inventoried in reference-contract.json and mapped with all nine dimensions documented or sourced not-applicable. Unchanged main-thread members are deliberately delegated to MDN/spec with links, per the delta-page scope stated in the contract notes.

The page answers the two questions the brief flagged as essential: what 'frame' means without rendering (a congested moment of the worker event loop; at-a-glance row + what-changes-in-workers table) and which fields are meaningful off-main-thread (field-by-field table on worker-entries/, including blockingDuration's redefinition and the zeroed rendering fields). The prototype-vs-proposal boundary is stated in the warn-block and repeated where relevant. Genuine ambiguity is kept explicit: the chromestatus summary describes a single-long-task prototype while the current WPT suite already exercises flood coalescing - the page reports both with sources rather than picking one.

Worker-side observer registration (explainer pattern), a minimal reproducible congestion trigger (derived from the WPT long-task scenario: long handler + backlogged second message), a shape-classification example for scriptCount, and the WPT feature-detection pattern quoted verbatim. All in semantic <pre><code>. Not runtime-executed: this environment's headless Chromium was not run with the flag to observe real entries, so examples are source-derived (the WPT suite is cited as the executable evidence).

Honest interim tables on all three pages: Chrome dev trial 153 behind the exact flag; Edge/Firefox/Safari 'no signal' per the ChromeStatus record's vendor views; parent main-thread LoAF context (Chrome/Edge 123, Baseline limited) cited to BCD and webstatus.dev. guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation tables without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on intrinsic sizing; wrap potentially-wide content in overflow containers; overflow-wrap on unbreakable tokens; flex-wrap for wrapping rows.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: every data table sits in .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}; overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1, lede, code and table cells; <wbr> in the scriptCount H1; baseline-browsers list uses flex-wrap; pre blocks scroll internally. Exception: no container queries - the single-column editorial measure matches prior accepted pages.

guidanceConsulted.query: embedding third-party iframe demo lazy loading performance
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: LoAF-specific guidance: observe with buffered:true so pre-registration frames are not lost; aggregate scripts by sourceURL; filter noise with thresholds before reporting.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied to the page's code examples: every observer example uses buffered:true, iterates entry.scripts for sourceURL/sourceFunctionName attribution, and the scriptCount example filters by shape before warning - keeping the documented patterns consistent with the guidance's recommended LoAF usage. Also applied loading="lazy" to the embedded showcase iframe (from the optimize-image-priority hit in the same search: deprioritize non-critical below-the-fold embeds).

openQuestions: The ChromeStatus summary (2026-08-04) says the prototype reports 'a single long task' with floods as follow-up, but the WPT suite in the tree already asserts flood coalescing and idle-gap boundaries. The page presents both with sources; re-check after the next milestone whether the summary or the implementation moved.
Whether PerformanceObserver.supportedEntryTypes includes 'long-animation-frame' in worker scope under the flag was not verifiable from the fetched sources and is deliberately not claimed anywhere.

The pauseDuration semantics for worker-only synchronous APIs (e.g. sync XHR in workers, Atomics.wait) are not spelled out in any fetched source; the page lists pauseDuration as present but does not enumerate which worker operations count.
